title: Copilot Studio: cost controls in the Microsoft 365 admin center
summary: Hold: the governance checklist tells readers to assign AI Administrator or AI Reader after deciding who will create and edit policies, although the cited setup documentation says these roles cannot create policies. The opt-in behaviour, billing arrangements and listed control paths are supported; the checklist needs to distinguish creators, editors and readers.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: The documentation does not specify exactly what happens to a covered agent when a Microsoft 365 resource-policy spending limit is reached.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio resource-based limit is reached; resource-based spending reached Copilot. Opened feature and Managing AI experiences pages; the latter describes loss of access under identity policies, not the resource-policy agent stopping behaviour.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, first bullet
claims.claim: After deciding who will create and edit resource-based policies, assigning AI Administrator or AI Reader accordingly supplies the needed roles.
claims.quote: AI administrator and License administrator roles can edit spending policies, manage limits and alerts, and billing methods. However, they can't create spending policies.
claims.fix: Replace the bullet with: 'Separate policy creators, editors and consumption readers. The setup page lists Global administrator or Billing administrator for initial policy creation; AI Administrator can edit policies, and AI Reader can only view consumption. Confirm resource-policy creation permissions in your tenant before piloting, because the feature page recommends AI Administrator for management but the setup page explicitly excludes creation.' Keep the existing documentation-disagreement note.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist asks administrators to assign Microsoft 365 roles, but the controls table has no row for role assignment.
claims.quote: Before rollout: 'then assign AI Administrator or AI Reader accordingly.' The four control rows cover resource policies, capacity allocation, agent limits and pay-as-you-go billing plans, not role assignment.
claims.fix: Add a controls row for 'Assignment of Microsoft 365 policy-management and consumption-reader roles', with the documented role-assignment UI and automation surface researched separately. Preserve the distinction between policy creators, editors and readers.
